note: HYPOTHETICAL scenarios for illustration only. Not reports, not forecasts. Kept out of the feed, alerts and sentiment. Locations are public, widely reported sites; estimates are marked and their basis shown.

items.title: US nuclear strike on Pickaxe Mountain
items.claim: Tucker Carlson claimed on 1 Nov 2026 (citing an unnamed "informed observer") that the US might use a nuclear weapon on Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La. No US or Israeli official confirmed it; Trump said on 16 Oct 2026 he "wouldn't use nuclear". Fact-checkers rate the claim unproven/misleading.
items.trigger: pickaxe|kolang|nuclear strike on iran|nuke iran|nuclear option

target.name: Kuh-e Kolang Gaz La (Pickaxe Mountain), ~2 km south of Natanz

items.yield_note: Assumption: 360 kt, the publicly stated maximum yield of the US B61-13 gravity bomb. Real choices could be far lower or higher.

fallout.note: Surface bursts loft soil into a fallout plume. Its length and direction depend on the winds on the day; the plume shown points east only to illustrate shape, it is not a forecast.

effects: Markets would price a major supply-risk shock; Gulf exports pass through Hormuz (~20 mb/d, ~20% of world consumption, EIA/IEA 2025).
War-risk insurance and rerouting would likely spike across the Gulf and Red Sea.
First nuclear use since 1945; experts quoted by Snopes and CSIS warn of region-wide retaliation and a proliferation cascade.
Fallout over central Iran; contamination extent depends on yield, depth and weather (Glasstone & Dolan ch. 9).
ladder: Iranian missile retaliation on US bases & Israel
sources: Snopes: Is Trump admin planning nuclear strike on Iran? (5 Nov 2026)
Glasstone & Dolan, The Effects of Nuclear Weapons (1977), OSTI

items.title: Conventional bunker-buster strike on Pickaxe / Fordow
items.claim: Trump said (16 Oct 2026) the US might still "take a shot" at Pickaxe with conventional ordnance. In June 2025 (Operation Midnight Hammer) B-2s dropped GBU-57 MOPs on Fordow; CSIS counted six double-tapped craters.
items.weapon: GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrator (30,000 lb; public specs)
facts: GBU-57: ~30,000 lb penetrator; public reporting rates it to penetrate roughly 60 m of earth before detonating.
Public estimates put Pickaxe tunnels 80–100 m deep in granite (CNS 2023, cited by CSIS) — deeper and harder rock than Fordow.
CSIS: the June 2025 strike on Fordow used 12 MOPs on six aim points (ventilation shafts).
effects: Brent typically jumps on strike headlines; in June 2025 it fell 7% once Iran's retaliation proved limited (Reuters).
Iran retaliated in 2025 with 19 missiles at Al Udeid (Qatar MoD); similar or larger response possible.
Damage likely partial: depth may exceed MOP reach; entrances and power could be cut (CSIS).
sources: CSIS: Damage to Iran's nuclear program
Reuters: Iran fires missiles at US base in Qatar (2025)

items.title: Iran mines / closes the Strait of Hormuz
items.claim: Iran's IRGC has said tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the strait (Nov 2026 reports) and Iranian officials have said Hormuz "will stay shut".
items.weapon: Naval mines, fast boats, anti-ship missiles (illustrative)
effects: ~20 mb/d (≈20% of world consumption) moved through Hormuz in 2025; only 3.5–5.5 mb/d of bypass pipeline capacity (IEA).
About one-fifth of global LNG trade transits the strait (EIA), mainly Qatar.
Tanker traffic halts; insurers cancel war-risk cover; Asia (≈80% of flows) hit hardest.
US/allied mine-clearing and escort operations would follow.
ladder: US mine-clearing & strikes on IRGC Navy

items.title: Strikes on Gulf energy infrastructure
items.claim: Precedent: on 14 Sep 2019 drones and cruise missiles hit Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq and Khurais, briefly halting 5.7 mb/d — about half of Saudi output (Reuters).
effects: 2019 precedent removed ~5.7 mb/d briefly; Reuters reported it left the world without spare capacity.
Ras Laffan is Qatar's LNG hub; outages would tighten Europe and Asia gas.
Gulf states could join or restrain US action; reciprocal strikes on Iranian energy (e.g. Kharg) possible.
sources: Reuters: Attacks on Saudi oil facilities knock out half supply (2019)
Reuters: Attack leaves world without spare capacity

items.title: Iranian missile barrage on US bases
items.claim: Precedent: on 23 Jun 2025 Iran fired 19 missiles at Al Udeid, Qatar; Qatar said 18 were intercepted and one landed inside the base without casualties (Qatar MoD via Janes/Al Jazeera).
items.trigger: al udeid|us bases?|us base|ballistic missiles? at|retaliat
effects: Brent fell 7% after the limited 2025 attack (Reuters) — markets react to whether retaliation is contained.
Gulf airspace closures (Qatar, Bahrain, UAE) as in June 2025.
US casualties would sharply raise pressure for wider strikes.
sources: Reuters: Iran fires missiles at US base in Qatar
Janes: Qatari, US air defences defeat Iranian attack
Al Jazeera: Tehran attacks US base in Qatar

items.title: Large Hezbollah rocket barrage on Haifa
items.claim: Precedent: in Oct 2024 Hezbollah fired heavy rocket salvos at Haifa, including the first direct hits on the city (Reuters, 6 Oct 2024).
items.weapon: Unguided rockets and some guided missiles
effects: Schools closed and shelters opened in northern Israel in 2024.
Israeli retaliation on Beirut's Dahiyeh and south Lebanon likely.

items.title: Israeli air campaign on Beirut's southern suburbs
items.claim: Precedent: Israel's 2024 strikes on Dahiyeh, Beirut, including the Sept 2024 strike that killed Hassan Nasrallah.
effects: Mass displacement from southern Beirut as in autumn 2024.
Hezbollah long-range fire at central Israel possible.
sources: Reuters: Hezbollah rockets hit Haifa (context of 2024 escalation)

items.title: Oreshnik IRBM strike on Kyiv
items.claim: Precedent: on 21 Nov 2024 Russia fired its new Oreshnik intermediate-range ballistic missile at Dnipro, launched from Astrakhan region ~700 km away, with multiple warheads (Reuters).
effects: Russia framed Oreshnik as a warning to the West; NATO consultations likely.
Few systems can intercept IRBM-class warheads.
sources: Reuters: Russia fired new ballistic missile at Ukraine (2024)

items.title: Winter strike wave on Ukraine's power grid
items.claim: Russia has repeatedly struck Ukrainian power infrastructure in winter; the IAEA has reported drone strikes affecting staff and power lines at nuclear plants.
effects: Rolling blackouts and heating loss for millions in winter.
IAEA warns about strikes near nuclear plants.
ladder: Retaliatory Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries

items.title: Houthi missile hits tanker in Bab el-Mandeb
items.claim: The Houthis have repeatedly attacked shipping since late 2023; CSIS notes tanker attacks can choke Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export route.
effects: Bab el-Mandeb oil flows fell from 8.0 mb/d (2022) to ~4.1 mb/d (2024) as ships rerouted around the Cape (EIA).
Tanker hits raise freight and insurance costs.
sources: CSIS: Global economic consequences of Red Sea attacks

items.title: US/Israeli strikes on Hodeidah port
items.claim: Hodeidah port and Ras Isa have been struck repeatedly since 2024 in response to Houthi attacks.
effects: Hodeidah handles much of Yemen's food and fuel imports.
Houthi retaliation on Israel and shipping.
sources: CSIS: Houthi aggression and a roadmap for peace

items.title: Renewed India–Pakistan missile exchange
items.claim: Precedent: on 7 May 2025 India's Operation Sindoor struck nine sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir; Pakistan said six locations were hit and retaliated (Reuters).
effects: Both states are nuclear-armed; 2025 fighting ended in a ceasefire after four days.
sources: Reuters: What targets did India say it destroyed?

items.title: India restricts Indus river flows
items.claim: India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty in April 2025; Pakistan said any attempt to stop or divert its water would be treated as an "act of war" (Reuters).
effects: Pakistan's farm economy depends heavily on Indus-system water.
Pakistan has framed diversion as a casus belli.
sources: Reuters: What is the Indus Waters Treaty?
Reuters: Panic in Pakistan as India vows to cut off water

items.title: PLA blockade / quarantine of Taiwan
items.claim: CSIS ChinaPower and the CSIS 'Lights Out?' wargame study how China could blockade Taiwan, from coast-guard 'quarantine' to an all-out kinetic blockade.
effects: Taiwan makes most of the world's advanced semiconductors; supply chains would seize.
Taiwan imports almost all its energy; CSIS wargame examines how long it could hold out.
sources: CSIS ChinaPower: How China could blockade Taiwan
CSIS: Lights Out? Wargaming a Chinese blockade

items.title: PLA missile salvo into waters around Taiwan
items.claim: Precedent: in Aug 2022 the PLA fired ballistic missiles into zones around Taiwan during large-scale drills.
effects: Ships and flights reroute around closure zones.
sources: CSIS ChinaPower: How China could blockade Taiwan

items.title: North Korean seventh nuclear test
items.claim: Precedent: North Korea's sixth test at Punggye-ri on 3 Sep 2017 registered as a magnitude 6.3 event (USGS).
effects: ROK–US–Japan drills and strategic asset deployments.
sources: 38 North: Sixth nuclear test at Punggye-ri

items.title: Artillery shelling of a border island
items.claim: Precedent: on 23 Nov 2010 North Korea shelled Yeonpyeong Island, killing two South Korean marines and two civilians (BBC/Reuters).
effects: South Korea returned fire in 2010; a repeat could trigger air strikes.
Won and Korean stocks typically dip on border clashes.
sources: BBC: North Korean artillery hits South Korean island (2010)
Reuters: North Korea shells South in fiercest attack in decades
